accuracy.evidence: Checked against the English National Curriculum Year 1 spelling requirements (segment spoken words into phonemes and spell words containing the phonemes taught) and Common Core L.K.2d and L.1.2e. Every phoneme count was checked by hand: cat 3, ship 3 (sh), frog 4, egg 2 (gg is one phoneme), fish 3, tent 4, duck 3 (ck), chick 3 (ch, ck), milk 4, ring 3 (ng), chop 3. Clusters are taught as two phonemes, digraphs as one, so no simplification is wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-spelling errors: one box per letter instead of per sound (ship prediction, egg and fish strip feedback, duck challenge), leaving out the medial vowel (cat prediction, middle-box step, pt for pot and bd for bed items), dropping the second consonant of a cluster (fog for frog prediction, stop and hand repairs, sop challenge), splitting a digraph (s then h tile feedback) and writing letter names (bee you ess challenge, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsegbox is built on Elkonin sound boxes for spelling: strips with 2, 3 or 4 boxes matched to a spoken word, an empty middle box that takes a vowel tile, a lost-sound repair inside a cluster, and left-to-right box filling where sh, ck and ch tiles fill one box. It runs the opposite way to the blending lab (sounds to letters, not letters to a word); highest 6-token overlap with any other flagship is 9% (flag_fback, shared shell code).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea by acting before the text names it: picking 4 boxes for ship is answered with sh is one sound so one box; dropping e into c?t says c-e-t is not cat and names the middle sound; putting g into fr?g reads back the wrong word; tapping s for ship explains that sh goes in one box as one tile. Each step's done message states the rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the task then disproves: 4 boxes for 4 letters in ship (the strip shows 3), ct is fine for cat (no word works without its vowel), fog is right for frog (the empty box shows the lost r), and s then h for ship (the sh tile fills one box). The done message reports the prediction back.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with shuffled options and a separate message for every wrong option, e.g. every word has a vowel sound, so o needs a box; sh and ck are one sound each; op is two sounds, o and p; the t comes right after s and you hear it; the name bee is not the sound. Wrong taps in the lab also read back the wrong word, such as c-e-t is not cat.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation scores Flesch-Kincaid grade 0.1 and the adult text 6.8, inside the family limits of 5.0 and 10.0. Canvas sentences are short, the target words are decodable CVC, CCVC and CVCC words, and the term segmenting is defined in the first step and contrasted with blending.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a rule, a count or a mistake to watch for. The explanation is under 1% the same as Blending Sounds to Read Words, the nearest lesson, and each done message states the specific rule found (count sounds not letters, every word needs its vowel, both cluster sounds get a box).

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of every step in dark and light: three box strips fit side by side, five vowel tiles fit one row, four sound boxes for frog, stop and tent fit with the picture above, and five spelling tiles fit one row. Every tile is at least 60 px wide and 64 px tall with a large button twin below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: all four tasks finish with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, and axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme, with no console errors. Every drag has a labelled button twin, e.g. Put a in the middle box of cat, and each result is spoken through the live region and the canvas aria-label.

sources: DfE (2013) English programmes of study, Key Stage 1, Year 1 statutory spelling requirements and Appendix 1 (segmenting spoken words into phonemes; digraphs, adjacent consonants)
Common Core State Standards ELA L.K.2d and L.1.2e (spell simple and untaught words phonetically)
DfE (2021) Choosing a phonics teaching programme: core criteria (blending for reading, segmenting for spelling; phoneme and grapheme terminology)
